title: Cheque bounce notice
description: A Section 138 demand after a cheque was returned for insufficient funds.
text:
SETHI & ASSOCIATES
Advocates & Legal Consultants
Office: 204, Court Chambers, MG Road, Pune 411001

LEGAL NOTICE UNDER SECTION 138 OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881

Date: {{days_ago:9}}

To,
Mr. Rahul Sharma,
Flat 4B, Green Park Society,
Pune 411045

Under instructions from our client, ABC Finance Ltd., we serve you the following notice.

1. You had issued cheque bearing No. 123456 dated {{days_ago:24}} for Rs. 1,85,000 drawn on State Bank of India, FC Road Branch, Pune, in favour of our client towards repayment of a business loan.

2. The said cheque was presented for payment on {{days_ago:17}} and was returned unpaid on {{days_ago:15}} with the bank remark "insufficient funds". A copy of the cheque return memo is enclosed.

3. Despite repeated requests, you have failed and neglected to pay the said amount of Rs. 1,85,000.

4. You are hereby called upon to pay the said amount of Rs. 1,85,000 within 15 days of receipt of this notice, failing which our client shall be constrained to initiate criminal proceedings against you under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences.

Yours faithfully,
P. R. Deshmukh
Advocate for ABC Finance Ltd.

title: Rent and eviction notice
description: A landlord demands arrears and asks a tenant to vacate within 30 days.
text:
NOTICE TO QUIT AND DEMAND FOR ARREARS OF RENT

Date: {{days_ago:12}}

From:
Mr. Suresh Patil,
Owner, Shop No. 7, Laxmi Complex,
Station Road, Nashik 422001

To:
Ms. Farida Khan,
Proprietor, New Look Tailors,
Shop No. 7, Laxmi Complex,
Station Road, Nashik 422001

Sir / Madam,

You are a tenant of the above shop under a lease agreement dated {{days_ago:700}}. The monthly rent is Rs. 24,000 payable on or before the 5th day of every English calendar month.

You have failed to pay rent for the months of August, September and October. A sum of Rs. 72,000 is due as arrears of rent. You have also failed to pay the maintenance charges of Rs. 9,000.

Despite oral requests and WhatsApp messages, you have not cleared the arrears. You have also sub-let a portion of the premises without my written consent, which is contrary to the lease agreement and the applicable rent control law.

I therefore call upon you to pay the arrears of Rs. 81,000 within 30 days and to vacate the premises on or before {{days_ahead:30}}. If you fail to comply, I shall be compelled to file an eviction suit and a recovery case before the competent civil court and to claim mesne profits and costs.

Please treat this as a formal notice under the applicable rent control law and the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.

Yours faithfully,
Suresh Patil
Owner

title: Loan recovery notice
description: A lender recalls an overdue personal loan and warns of recovery action.
text:
ARIHANT HOUSING FINANCE LIMITED
Registered Office: 3rd Floor, Trade Centre, Andheri East, Mumbai 400069

LOAN RECALL AND DEMAND NOTICE

Date: {{days_ago:8}}

To,
Mr. Vikram Nair,
B-1204, Palm Grove Apartments,
Sector 21, Navi Mumbai 400705

Loan Account No.: AHF-PL-884210

Dear Sir,

We refer to the personal loan of Rs. 6,50,000 sanctioned to you on {{days_ago:420}}. The loan is repayable in 48 equated monthly instalments of Rs. 17,240.

As on the date of this notice, instalments for the months of July, August and September remain unpaid. The total outstanding, including principal, accrued interest and late payment charges, is Rs. 2,48,500. A statement of account is enclosed.

Despite our reminders and calls, you have not regularised the account. Your loan account is therefore classified as a non-performing asset in accordance with RBI recovery norms.

You are hereby called upon to pay the outstanding amount of Rs. 2,48,500 within 15 days of receipt of this notice. If you fail to do so, we shall be entitled to initiate recovery action, arbitration under the loan agreement, and such other proceedings as may be available in law, including action under the SARFAESI Act, 2002 where applicable.

If you dispute the amount, write to us with the supporting documents within the said period. Do not deal with any recovery agent who cannot produce written authorisation from the company.

Yours faithfully,
Arihant Housing Finance Limited
Authorised Signatory

title: Consumer complaint notice
description: A buyer demands a refund for a defective refrigerator before approaching the consumer commission.
text:
LEGAL NOTICE UNDER THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019

Date: {{days_ago:6}}

From:
Ms. Neha Kulkarni,
12, Shivaji Nagar, Nagpur 440010

To:
The Manager,
CoolHome Appliances Pvt. Ltd.,
Ground Floor, Sitabuldi Market, Nagpur 440012

Subject: Defective refrigerator and demand for refund of Rs. 48,000

Madam / Sir,

I purchased a 320-litre refrigerator from your showroom on {{days_ago:95}} for Rs. 48,000. The invoice and the two-year warranty card are enclosed.

Within three weeks of delivery, the refrigerator stopped cooling. Your service technician visited on three occasions but could not repair the defect. The compressor was replaced once, yet the problem continues. The product is therefore defective and not fit for its ordinary purpose.

I have sent you emails on {{days_ago:60}} and {{days_ago:32}} and visited your showroom twice. You have neither replaced the product nor refunded the amount. This is a deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice.

I hereby call upon you to refund Rs. 48,000 together with compensation of Rs. 10,000 for the trouble and expense caused to me within 15 days of receiving this notice. If you fail to comply, I shall file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 through the e-Daakhil portal, entirely at your risk as to costs.

Yours faithfully,
Neha Kulkarni

title: Maintenance demand notice
description: A spouse claims monthly maintenance and warns of a family court case.
text:
LEGAL NOTICE FOR MAINTENANCE

Date: {{days_ago:11}}

From:
Mrs. Anjali Verma,
C/o Shakti Legal Aid Centre,
Civil Lines, Jaipur 302006

To:
Mr. Rohit Verma,
45, Rajendra Nagar,
Jaipur 302004

Subject: Demand for monthly maintenance under Section 144 BNSS, 2023

Sir,

You are the husband of my client, Mrs. Anjali Verma. You were married on {{days_ago:2200}} and have two minor children from the marriage, aged 7 and 4 years.

You left the matrimonial home on {{days_ago:400}} and have not provided any financial support since then. My client has no independent income and is presently living with her parents. The children are studying in a municipal school and their monthly expenses, including school fees, medicines and rent, exceed Rs. 28,000.

You are employed as a senior engineer and are earning approximately Rs. 1,10,000 per month. Despite repeated requests, you have paid nothing towards the maintenance of your wife and children.

My client therefore calls upon you to pay Rs. 18,000 per month as maintenance for herself and the two children with effect from the date of this notice, and to clear the arrears of the last six months amounting to Rs. 1,08,000 within 15 days.

If you fail to comply, my client shall be constrained to file an application under Section 144 of the BNSS, 2023 and the applicable family law before the Family Court, Jaipur, and to seek interim maintenance and costs.

Yours faithfully,
Adv. Meera Singh
For Shakti Legal Aid Centre

title: Property possession notice
description: A neighbour alleges encroachment and demands removal of construction.
text:
LEGAL NOTICE REGARDING ENCROACHMENT AND POSSESSION

Date: {{days_ago:7}}

From:
Mr. Mahesh Deshpande,
Plot No. 14, Vidya Nagar, Kolhapur 416001

To:
Mr. Imran Shaikh,
Plot No. 15, Vidya Nagar, Kolhapur 416001

Sir,

I am the absolute owner of Plot No. 14, Vidya Nagar, Kolhapur, by virtue of a registered sale deed dated {{days_ago:3000}}. The property tax receipts and mutation entries are in my name.

You are the owner of the adjoining Plot No. 15. During recent construction, you have extended a boundary wall and a staircase approximately four feet into my plot. This is an encroachment on my property and interferes with my right to peaceful possession and enjoyment.

I obtained a survey map from the Talathi office on {{days_ago:40}}, which confirms that the constructed portion falls within my plot. Photographs of the encroachment are enclosed.

I hereby call upon you to remove the unauthorised construction and restore the boundary to its original position within 15 days of receiving this notice. You are also directed not to create any third-party interest in the disputed portion.

If you fail to comply, I shall be constrained to file a civil suit for declaration, possession, mandatory injunction and damages before the competent civil court under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and the Specific Relief Act, 1963.

Yours faithfully,
Mahesh Deshpande

title: Unpaid salary notice
description: An employee demands unpaid wages and challenges a termination without notice.
text:
LEGAL NOTICE FOR UNPAID SALARY AND WRONGFUL TERMINATION

Date: {{days_ago:10}}

From:
Mr. Arjun Rao,
H.No. 8-2-293, Jubilee Hills,
Hyderabad 500033

To:
The Managing Director,
Nova Digital Services Pvt. Ltd.,
Plot 12, HITEC City,
Hyderabad 500081

Subject: Unpaid salary of Rs. 1,26,000 and termination without notice

Sir,

I was employed with your company as a Senior Analyst from {{days_ago:900}} under an appointment letter dated {{days_ago:895}}. My last drawn salary was Rs. 63,000 per month.

My salary for the months of August and September has not been paid, amounting to Rs. 1,26,000. Despite repeated emails to the HR department, no payment has been made. My salary slips and bank statements are enclosed.

On {{days_ago:20}}, I was informed by email that my services were terminated with immediate effect. The appointment letter requires one month's notice or payment in lieu, neither of which was given. No domestic enquiry was conducted and no reason was recorded.

I therefore call upon you to pay Rs. 1,26,000 towards unpaid salary and Rs. 63,000 towards salary in lieu of notice, totalling Rs. 1,89,000, within 15 days of receiving this notice. I also reserve my right to claim compensation for wrongful termination.

If you fail to comply, I shall approach the Labour Commissioner and initiate proceedings under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and the applicable state labour law.

Yours faithfully,
Arjun Rao

title: GST mismatch notice
description: A tax notice asks for a response to a GST return mismatch within 30 days.
text:
OFFICE OF THE ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER OF STATE TAX
GST Division, 4th Floor, Vanijya Bhavan, Ahmedabad 380009

NOTICE UNDER SECTION 61 OF THE CGST ACT, 2017

Reference No.: GST/SCN/2026/1842
Date: {{days_ago:5}}

To,
M/s Shreeji Traders,
GSTIN: 24ABCDE1234F1Z5,
12, Relief Road, Ahmedabad 380001

Subject: Discrepancy in GSTR-3B and GSTR-2B for the period April 2024 to March 2025

Sir / Madam,

On scrutiny of your returns for the financial year 2024-25, it is observed that the input tax credit claimed in GSTR-3B exceeds the credit available in GSTR-2B by Rs. 3,42,800. There also appears to be a short payment of output tax of Rs. 86,400 for the month of January 2025.

You are hereby directed to explain the discrepancy and submit a reconciliation statement along with copies of the relevant invoices and returns. If the explanation is not found satisfactory, proceedings for demand and penalty may be initiated under the CGST Act, 2017.

You are requested to file your response on the GST portal within 30 days of the date of this notice. Please quote the reference number in all correspondence. This notice is generated electronically and does not require a physical signature.

Yours faithfully,
Assistant Commissioner of State Tax
GST Division, Ahmedabad

title: Unpaid professional fees
description: A consultant demands unpaid fees before filing a civil suit.
text:
LEGAL NOTICE FOR RECOVERY OF PROFESSIONAL FEES

Date: {{days_ago:9}}

From:
M/s Insight Design Studio LLP,
3rd Floor, Design House, Banjara Hills,
Hyderabad 500034

To:
Mr. Karan Mehta,
Managing Director, Brightline Foods Pvt. Ltd.,
Plot 44, Industrial Estate, Hyderabad 500032

Sir,

Under instructions from my client, M/s Insight Design Studio LLP, I serve you this notice.

My client provided branding and packaging design services to your company under an agreement dated {{days_ago:240}}. All deliverables were completed and approved by your team on {{days_ago:90}}. The agreed professional fee was Rs. 2,40,000, of which Rs. 95,000 remains unpaid despite three invoices and repeated reminders.

You have neither raised any quality dispute in writing nor paid the balance. My client has therefore instructed me to demand the outstanding amount of Rs. 95,000 along with interest at 12% per annum from the due date.

You are hereby called upon to pay Rs. 95,000 together with interest within 15 days of receiving this notice. If you fail to do so, my client shall be constrained to file a civil suit for recovery before the competent court, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences.

Yours faithfully,
Adv. Ritu Malhotra
For Insight Design Studio LLP
